subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A spacecraft moves through deep space with its engines off and no resultant force acting. According to Newton's first law, what happens?
options: It continues at constant velocity in a straight line
It gradually slows down and stops
It immediately falls
It speeds up
questions.explain: Newton's first law: with no resultant force, an object continues at constant velocity (here in a straight line at steady speed). This tendency to keep its motion is called inertia.

questions.q: Which of these is the correct SI base unit of mass?
options: Gram
Newton
Pound
Kilogram
questions.explain: The SI base unit of mass is the kilogram (kg). The gram is a smaller unit, the newton is the unit of force, and the pound is not an SI unit.

questions.q: When light passes from glass into air (along a line not on the normal), it bends:
options: Away from the normal because it speeds up
Towards the normal because it slows down
It does not bend at all
Back the way it came
questions.explain: Light speeds up when it enters a less dense medium (glass to air), so it refracts away from the normal.

questions.q: A ball is thrown straight up. As it rises (before reaching the top), which energy transfer mainly occurs?
options: Gravitational potential to kinetic
Thermal to kinetic
Chemical to kinetic
Kinetic to gravitational potential
questions.explain: As the ball rises it slows down, so its kinetic store falls while its gravitational potential store rises: energy is transferred from kinetic to gravitational potential.

questions.q: Why does atmospheric pressure decrease as you go higher up a mountain?
options: The air becomes a liquid
Gravity disappears at altitude
There is less air (a shorter column of air) above you pressing down
The air gets colder
questions.explain: Atmospheric pressure is caused by the weight of the air above. Higher up, there is less air above you and it is less dense, so the pressure is lower.

questions.q: In the required practical, how can you measure the speed of waves in a ripple tank?
options: Measure only the depth of water
Time how long the tank takes to fill
Measure the amplitude and double it
Measure the frequency and wavelength, then use v = fλ
questions.explain: You find the frequency (e.g. from the wave generator or by counting waves per second) and the wavelength (e.g. from a stroboscope or by measuring several waves), then calculate v = fλ.

questions.q: For a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature, the volume is halved. According to pV = constant, the new pressure is...
options: doubled
halved
unchanged
quartered
questions.explain: At constant temperature pV is constant, so if V is halved, p must double to keep the product the same (Boyle's law).

questions.q: Heating a substance without changing its state increases its internal energy. Specifically, it increases the particles'...
options: mass
potential energy only, so temperature stays constant
number
kinetic energy, so the temperature rises
questions.explain: When heating raises temperature (no state change), the energy increases the particles' kinetic energy, so they move faster and the temperature rises.

questions.q: An object floats when the upthrust acting on it is:
options: Equal to its weight
Always greater than its weight
Less than its weight
Zero
questions.explain: When floating, the upthrust (upward force from the fluid) balances the object's weight, so the resultant force is zero. If weight exceeds the maximum upthrust, the object sinks.

questions.q: Which method would best reduce unwanted energy transfers between a machine's moving parts?
options: Increasing the temperature
Painting it black
Lubrication
Adding more mass
questions.explain: Lubrication reduces friction between moving parts, reducing energy dissipated to the thermal store. Insulation and streamlining are other valid methods of reducing unwanted transfers.

questions.q: What is the key difference between an alternator and a dynamo?
options: An alternator uses slip rings and produces ac; a dynamo uses a split-ring commutator and produces dc
A dynamo uses no magnets
An alternator produces direct current (dc); a dynamo produces alternating current (ac)
They are identical in every way
questions.explain: An alternator uses slip rings, giving alternating current (ac). A dynamo uses a split-ring commutator, which reverses the connections each half turn to give direct current (dc).

questions.q: What happens to parallel rays of light after they pass through a converging (convex) lens?
options: They are brought together at the principal focus
They are absorbed by the lens
They stay parallel
They spread out as if from a point behind the lens
questions.explain: A converging lens refracts parallel rays so that they meet at the principal focus (focal point). A diverging lens, by contrast, spreads parallel rays out.

questions.q: An object moves at a steady speed in a circular orbit. Why is it still accelerating?
options: Its speed is increasing
Its direction (and therefore velocity) is constantly changing
It is moving in a straight line
It is not accelerating
questions.explain: Velocity is a vector. Even at constant speed, the direction is continuously changing in a circular orbit, so the velocity changes — this change in velocity is the (centripetal) acceleration.

questions.q: What is the difference between the mass and the weight of an object?
options: Mass is the amount of matter (kg); weight is the gravitational force on it (N)
Mass and weight are the same thing
Mass is measured in newtons; weight in kilograms
Weight never changes but mass depends on location
questions.explain: Mass is the amount of matter (in kg) and is constant. Weight is the gravitational force on that mass (in N) and depends on the gravitational field strength, so it changes between the Earth and the Moon.

questions.q: What is the difference between elastic and inelastic deformation?
options: Elastic deformation is permanent; inelastic returns to shape
Inelastic only happens to metals
They are the same thing
Elastic deformation returns to the original shape when the force is removed; inelastic does not
questions.explain: In elastic deformation the object returns to its original shape once the force is removed. In inelastic (plastic) deformation it does not fully return — it is permanently changed.

questions.q: What is meant by the internal energy of a system?
options: Only the potential energy stored between particles
The energy supplied by an external heater
The total kinetic energy and potential energy of all the particles
Only the kinetic energy of the particles
questions.explain: Internal energy is the total energy stored by the particles: the sum of their kinetic energy (from motion) and the potential energy stored in the bonds/forces between them.

questions.q: Which statement about permanent and induced magnets is correct?
options: A permanent magnet loses its magnetism as soon as it is moved away from iron
Induced magnetism produces a force of repulsion
An induced magnet only becomes magnetic in a magnetic field and quickly loses it when removed
An induced magnet always repels a permanent magnet
questions.explain: Induced magnetism appears only while a material is in a magnetic field and is lost (or much reduced) when removed. Induced magnets always cause attraction, never repulsion.

questions.q: Which change would NOT increase the strength of an electromagnet (solenoid)?
options: Increasing the current
Using a thicker plastic former with no iron
Adding an iron core
Adding more turns of wire
questions.explain: Electromagnet strength increases with more current, more turns and an iron core. A plastic former with no iron does not boost the field.

questions.q: What happens when an electron in an atom absorbs electromagnetic radiation of the right energy?
options: It moves to a lower energy level
It leaves the atom and becomes a neutron
It turns into a proton
It moves to a higher energy level (further from the nucleus)
questions.explain: Absorbing EM radiation can move an electron to a higher energy level. When it falls back to a lower level it emits EM radiation.

questions.q: Why does the national grid use step-up transformers before transmission over long distances?
options: To increase the voltage and reduce the current, which reduces energy lost as heat in the cables
To increase the current and reduce the voltage
To make the cables thicker
To convert ac to dc for transmission
questions.explain: Stepping up the p.d. reduces the current for the same power (P = VI). Lower current means much less energy wasted as heat in the resistance of the transmission cables (heating ∝ I²R).

questions.q: What is the role of a step-down transformer in the national grid?
options: It decreases the p.d. to a safe value for homes
It converts ac to dc
It increases the current in the transmission cables
It increases the p.d. before transmission
questions.explain: A step-down transformer reduces the high transmission potential difference to a safer, lower value (about 230 V) for use in homes. Step-up transformers raise the p.d. for transmission.

questions.q: Hooke's law states that, up to the limit of proportionality, the extension of a spring is:
options: Directly proportional to the force applied
Independent of the force
Inversely proportional to the force
Equal to the force
questions.explain: Hooke's law: extension is directly proportional to the force, so F = ke. This holds only up to the limit of proportionality, beyond which the relationship is no longer linear.
